title: Finite etale generators and bounded-above constructible resolutions
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a quasi-compact scheme with an affine open cover by spectra of rings whose ideals satisfy the ascending chain condition, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Work with sheaves of $A$-modules on its small etale site and their derived category [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $D^-_c(X,A)$ for complexes with constructible cohomology, vanishing in sufficiently large degrees [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Every $L\in D^-_c(X,A)$ with $\mathcal H^i(L)=0$ for $i>0$ has a representative $Q^\bullet$ concentrated in degrees $\leq0$ in which each term is a finite direct sum of sheaves $u_!A_U$ for separated etale finite-type maps $u:U\to X$ (a finite disjoint union is allowed), and the kernels and cokernels of its differentials are constructible. In particular one can arrange $Q^0=u_!A_U$. For the brutal truncation, the canonical short exact sequence is $0\to Q^0[0]\to Q^\bullet\to\sigma^{\leq-1}Q^\bullet\to0$, and hence there is a distinguished triangle
$$Q^0\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow \sigma^{\leq-1}Q^\bullet\longrightarrow Q^0[1],$$
where $\sigma^{\leq-1}$ has no terms, and therefore no cohomology, in degrees $\geq0$. No finite projective resolution or finite Tor dimension of a constructible sheaf is asserted.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.1, finite etale generators and Kashiwara--Schapira Lemma 13.2.1(b), p. 42. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For a cochain complex concentrated in degrees $\leq0$, the degree-zero term $Q^0[0]$ is a subcomplex and the quotient is the brutal truncation $\sigma^{\leq-1}Q^\bullet$. Thus degreewise there is a short exact sequence $0\to Q^0[0]\to Q^\bullet\to\sigma^{\leq-1}Q^\bullet\to0$. Localizing at quasi-isomorphisms gives the displayed triangle with $Q^\bullet$ replaced by its derived object $L$. The quotient has no terms in degrees $\geq0$, hence no cohomology there; the orientation is checked by the two-term complex $[A\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}A]$ in degrees $-1,0$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.1, p. 42; brutal-truncation triangle (corrected)

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above representative $K^\bullet$ of $L$ and shift it so that $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>0$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of finite direct sums of $u_!A_U$ for separated etale finite-type $u$. At each induction stage, the cohomology sheaves of the finite tail and of its mapping cone are constructible: the tail has only finitely many terms above the current degree, its term sheaves are constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible], and [thm-constructible-serre] gives closure under kernels, cokernels, extensions. The finite-generator lifting statement [lem-trf-constructible-generator-epimorphism] can therefore be applied whenever the target is one of these constructible cone cohomology sheaves.

source.place: Tag 05T7 (derived-lemma-subcategory-left-resolution), induction setup and constructibility specialization

proof.text:
Construct $Q^n$ and the comparison map in descending induction. Suppose the tail $Q_{>n}=\sigma^{\geq n+1}Q$ and its map to $K^\bullet$ have been constructed, with the cone acyclic in degrees $>n$. Form the cycle pullback sheaf
$$Z_n=\ker(d_Q^{n+1})\times_{K^{n+1}}K^n,$$
where the map from $\ker(d_Q^{n+1})$ to $K^{n+1}$ is the tail comparison. The standard cone calculation gives a canonical epimorphism $Z_n\twoheadrightarrow H^n(\operatorname{Cone}(Q_{>n}\to K))$. The source $Z_n$ need not be constructible, but the target is constructible by Step 2. Apply [lem-trf-constructible-generator-epimorphism] to this epimorphism: it supplies $Q^n\in\mathcal P$ and an epimorphic composite $Q^n\to Z_n\to H^n(\operatorname{Cone})$. The two projections of $Q^n\to Z_n$ define $d_Q^n:Q^n\to Q^{n+1}$ and $f^n:Q^n\to K^n$; the pullback equation gives $d_Q^{n+1}d_Q^n=0$ and the chain-map identity.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, downward fibre-product construction (derived.tex line 5302)

proof.text: The epimorphic composite onto $H^n(\operatorname{Cone})$ kills that cone cohomology, so the induction invariant extends from degrees $>n$ to degree $n$. Descending through all $n$ makes the cone of $Q^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ acyclic, hence the comparison is a quasi-isomorphism. Every term of $Q^\bullet$ is a finite sum of $u_!A_U$, and each such summand is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-free-sheaf-constructible]; [thm-constructible-serre] then makes the kernel and cokernel of every differential constructible. Combining the finitely many degree-zero summands into one finite disjoint union gives the asserted $u:U\to X$.

source.place: Tag 05T7, completion of the downward fibre-product induction and quasi-isomorphism verification

proof.text: Undoing the initial shift gives a representative concentrated in degrees $\leq0$ with the stated finite etale terms. The degree-zero subcomplex then gives the short exact sequence and distinguished triangle of Step 1. No finite projective resolution or finite Tor-dimension assertion is used.
